content.comment_body: Hello, I received two new [product_name] [article_no] units for testing this week, mainly to evaluate the web server functionality. I've connected the devices and a PC on a separate network. The PC can access and open the default web interface, but the interface doesn't fit standard operations. I want to upload a simplified HTML page intended for end users. Can I use a standard FTP client to upload my own page? Are there any alternative methods? I couldn't locate any relevant documentation.
Hi, It's not possible to change the default web page. User-created web pages are not supported. Wishing you all the best for the holidays.

I agree with the previous comments. The web interface generated by the [product_name] web server mimics the built-in screen, and it cannot be changed. You might want to consider switching to [version_no] for more flexibility.

Thank you for the feedback. It's unfortunate that custom pages aren't possible, it would have been a convenient solution. Sadly, [version_no] is beyond our budget. We use a large number of [product_name] units monthly, so cost is a major factor. I see there's now an option to connect the [product_name] to a panel. Is it possible to use this panel as an HMI display for multiple [product_name] [article_no] units? For example, a panel connected via VPNs to multiple [product_name] units.

Yes, you can connect up to seven [product_name] [article_no] modules in a network with an HMI screen from [company_name]. All devices need to be in the same subnet mask. You can design buttons on the HMI that communicate over the network with the [product_name] units and much more. You'll need certain models of HMI screens and the latest version of [product_name] engineering software.

Thanks for your answer and sorry for interrupting. After seeing the last question, I tested [product_name] configuration software and HMI software (latest version). Using a KTP700 Basic HMI and [product_name] controllers, I could connect four devices without issue, but I received an error when trying to connect a fifth (see attached image). I only have a basic software license and configured a basic HMI. Are seven connections only possible with a more advanced ('comfort') range of HMI panels, which also requires an upgraded license? Alternatively, is it possible to: link four [product_name] units to a basic display, and have those four units link onward to other [product_name] devices?

I'm just learning how to connect [product_name] to HMI screens. I have a KTP400 Basic HMI, plus a [product_name] [article_no] and another [product_name] [article_no], and it's working well. Signals transfer between devices successfully. However, when trying the same scenario you described, I could only connect three [product_name] units to the HMI screen.

I simulated the setup and it appears to work. One input is read and sent over the network to device 2, which stores the input in a memory block. You can use cascade wiring for these connections, but the network may become fragile—if one device goes offline, you lose information from the connected devices.

The restriction isn't due to the controller side. You should be able to connect up to seven units as discussed. The limitation comes from the HMI configuration, which matches what was previously mentioned.

That's related to the HMI screen. Using the specified engineering software (recent version), I could connect four [product_name] units to the KTP400 screen. Trying to add a fifth device causes an error message during compilation, stating that the HMI screen only supports four connections. However, you can configure a network with up to eight devices: for example, seven [product_name] units and one HMI. The HMI can directly connect to only four units. You can set up virtual connections linking additional units via one of the four connected devices. These virtual connections might allow signals to be sent or received to the HMI via intermediary devices. I'm not certain if this method will work in practice, but I plan to experiment with it.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members tested the limits and features of the [product_name] [article_no] web server and explored its integration with HMI panels. The built-in web interface does not allow user customization, and no method was found for uploading custom HTML pages. Technical discussions focused on how many [product_name] devices could be linked with basic HMI screens using standard engineering software, with a practical limit of four direct connections unless more advanced panels and software licenses are used. Some users considered virtual network setups to extend connectivity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the option to customize the web interface for simpler end-user interaction, as well as to connect a single HMI display to multiple controllers without major restrictions.
